question: To which of the following Gharanas did the Hindustani classical vocalist Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan belong?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Patiala Gharana.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was an Indian Hindustani classical vocalist, from the Patiala Gharana**.
 
• The most common epithet used to describe Ustad Ghulam Ali Khan is** 'Tansen of the 20th century.** Often referred to as Bade (older) Ghulam Ali Khan to differentiate him from other maestros of the same name.
 
• The genius musician was one of the most legendary** thumri vocalists** of all time, who took the Patiala Gharana.
 
• **Born on 2 April 1902 in Kasur (now in Pakistan),** Bade Ghulam Ali Khan belonged to a family of musicians.
 
• He was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Padma Bhushan in 1962 Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan breathed last on April 25, 1968, at Basheerbagh Palace in Hyderabad.**

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gwalior Gharana**:

 
 
• It is considered the oldest** Khyal Gharana in Indian classical music.**
 
• Gwalior Gharana was founded in the first half of the 19th century.
 
• Gwalior Gharana became popular in India during the reign of the Mughal emperor Akbar.
 
• Mian Tansen was one of the first and most famous vocalists who came from Gwalior.
 
• The word meaning of Gharana is “family" or "lineage".
 
• **The word Gharana was derived from the Sanskrit word Griha, which means "house'.**
 
• Gharana is a community of performers who share a distinctive musical style that traces to a particular instructor or region.
 
 
 
• **Kirana Gharana:**
 
 
• It is one of the most prominent Indian classical khayal gharanas and is associated mostly with the** perfect intonation of notes.**
 
• The gharana's style was further evolved and was established as one of the important styles in modern Indian classical music in the late **19th / early 20th centuries by the musicians Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan.**
 
• The name of this school of music comes from **Kirana or Kairana, a town and tehsil of Shamli District in Uttar Pradesh.**
